drivingQuestion: Does the gentile owner's unspecified intent invalidate a slaughter performed for him by a Jew, or does only the slaughterer's intent count?
outcomeNote: The mishna records the tannaitic dispute without deciding it; R' Yosei's a fortiori supports the anonymous ruling but no resolution is stated within this unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְנׇכְרִי – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹסֵל. אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אֲפִילּוּ שְׁחָטָהּ לֶאֱכוֹל לְנׇכְרִי מֵחֲצַר כָּבֵד שֶׁלָּהּ – פְּסוּלָה, שֶׁסְּתָם מַחְשֶׁבֶת נׇכְרִי לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of a Jew «who slaughters» the animal of a gentile «for a gentile, his slaughter is valid, and Rabbi Eliezer deems it not valid. Rabbi Eliezer says: Even if» the Jew «slaughtered» the animal with the intent «to feed the gentile from its diaphragm [meḥatzar kaved],» its slaughter is «not valid, as the unspecified intent of a gentile is» to slaughter the animal «for idol worship,» and it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הַדְּבָרִים, וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהַמַּחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁין – אֵין הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד, מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת בְּחוּלִּין – אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אֶלָּא אַחַר הַשּׁוֹחֵט?
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei says:» The «matter» of the intent of the gentile is irrelevant in this case, as can be derived by means of «an a fortiori» inference. «If in a place where intent» while slaughtering the animal «invalidates» the slaughter, i.e., «in sacrificial» animals, such as when slaughtering an offering with the intent to sacrifice it beyond its designated time, «everything follows only» the intent of the priest «performing the service» and not the intent of the owner, then «in a place where intent does not invalidate» the slaughter, i.e., «in non-sacred» animals, «is it not right that everything should follow only» the intent of «the one who slaughters» the animal?

moves.summary: The mishna rules that a Jew who slaughters an animal on a gentile's behalf has performed a valid slaughter.
moves.about: whether a Jew's slaughter of an animal on behalf of a gentile is valid despite the gentile owner's presumed idolatrous intent

moves.summary: R' Eliezer dissents and deems such slaughter invalid.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אליעזר: אפילו שחטה לאכול לנכרי
moves.summary: R' Eliezer extends his invalidation even to slaughter intended only to feed the gentile from the diaphragm, because a gentile's unspecified intent is for idol worship.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוסי: קל וחומר הדברים
moves.summary: R' Yosei argues a fortiori from sacrificial animals — where intent does invalidate yet only the officiant's intent counts — that in non-sacred animals everything follows the slaughterer, not the owner.
moves.about: whether the gentile owner's intent, or only the Jewish slaughterer's, determines the validity of the slaughter
